about: Known CPU faults the Night Watchman names as a posture tip (agent/desks/watchman-hw.php, watchmanHwCpuFault()). A fault applies when vendor, family and model match, the CPU's model name holds one of `names` as a whole word (when given), and its microcode is below `microcode_below`. A new known fault is one more entry in a release; one whose advice differs from the tip's words needs a tip of its own.

faults.name: Intel Vmin Shift Instability
sources: https://community.intel.com/t5/Processors/Intel-Core-13th-and-14th-Gen-Desktop-Instability-Root-Cause/m-p/1633442 (0x12B «must be loaded via BIOS update», it encompasses 0x125 and 0x129)
https://community.intel.com/t5/Processors/Intel-Core-13-14th-Gen-Instability-Update-Future-Products/m-p/1627440 (not affected: mobile incl. HX, i5 non-K, i3, Xeon, 12th Gen)

https://community.intel.com/t5/Mobile-and-Desktop-Processors/Additional-Warranty-Updates-on-Intel-Core-13th-14th-Gen-Desktop/td-p/1620853 (the 24 models: Intel's table is a picture; the names as the press transcribed it, gigazine.net 2024-08-07)
Model 183 (0xB7) alone is not enough: Intel's HX mobile and Xeon E parts share it and are not affected — the name decides (kernel intel-family.h, Intel's microcode release notes)
